sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日商业简报《DealBook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市DealBook峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的几位领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家能收听。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, House Republicans finally have everything they want.
sentences.zh: 今天，众议院共和党人终于得到了他们想要的一切。

sentences.en: Control of Congress, a Republican president, and a health care plan.
sentences.zh: 国会的控制权、一位共和党总统，以及一份医疗保健计划。

sentences.en: So why, as they head to a vote today, is the bill so disliked and the party so divided?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么在他们今天迎来投票之际，这项法案如此不受欢迎，党内又如此分裂？

sentences.en: And a view from the scene of yesterday's deadly attacks in London.
sentences.zh: 以及来自昨天伦敦致命袭击现场的报道。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月23日，星期四。

sentences.en: Thanks, Senator Burr.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，伯尔参议员。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: We start back in the summer of 2009.
sentences.zh: 我们把时间拨回2009年夏天。

sentences.en: The current tax treatment of health care, which is a relic of World War II, discriminates against the self-employed, against the unemployed,
sentences.zh: 现行的医疗保健税收政策是二战时期的遗留产物，它对个体经营者、失业人员,

sentences.en: and against those people who do not get health coverage at their jobs.
sentences.zh: 以及那些在工作中无法获得医疗保障的人并不公平。

sentences.en: This may have worked in America, when everybody had the same job throughout their lives and throughout their careers.
sentences.zh: 在过去，当每个人一生和职业生涯中都从事同一份工作时，这种模式在美国或许行得通。

sentences.en: That's not the America we have today.
sentences.zh: 但这已经不是我们今天所处的美国了。

sentences.en: Nearly a year before President Obama signed his plan for reforming American health care, a 39-year-old up-and-coming congressman, Paul Ryan,
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马总统签署其美国医改方案的近一年前，一位39岁的新星国会议员保罗·瑞恩,

sentences.en: introduced a Republican plan to overhaul the same system.
sentences.zh: 推出了一项旨在彻底改革同一系统的共和党方案。

sentences.en: You see, we already spend twice as much per person on health care in America than all the other industrialized countries.
sentences.zh: 要知道，我们在美国人均医疗保健上的花费已经是所有其他工业化国家的两倍。

sentences.en: The answer is to take the money we're already spending and spend it far more efficiently, far more effectively, to reflect the dynamics of the 21st century,
sentences.zh: 解决办法是将我们已经花费的资金进行更高效、更有效的使用，以反映21世纪的发展动态，

sentences.en: so that the center of this system is not politicians and bureaucrats making the decisions.
sentences.zh: 从而使这个系统的核心不再是做出决策的政客和官僚。

sentences.en: The center of this system is patients and their doctors making the decisions.
sentences.zh: 这个系统的核心应该是做出决策的患者和他们的医生。

sentences.en: But, back then, Democrats had control of everything.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，民主党人掌握了一切。

sentences.en: And it was their vision of health care that was enacted.
sentences.zh: 最终通过的是他们的医疗愿景。

sentences.en: Health care is a cancer in our government, and we're going to rip it out.
sentences.zh: 医保是我们政府肌体中的毒瘤，我们将把它彻底切除。

sentences.en: Almost as soon as it passed, Republicans voted to repeal it, more than 60 times.
sentences.zh: 几乎在该法案通过后不久，共和党人就投票试图废除它，次数超过60次。

sentences.en: And every time, they failed.
sentences.zh: 但每一次都以失败告终。

sentences.en: So they waited for nearly seven years.
sentences.zh: 于是他们等待了将近七年。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: Last night, and again this morning, I spoke with President-elect Donald Trump, and I congratulated him on his great victory.
sentences.zh: 昨晚和今天早上，我与当选总统唐纳德·特朗普进行了交谈，我祝贺他取得了伟大的胜利。

sentences.en: In a single night...
sentences.zh: 在一个夜晚之内……

sentences.en: We talked about the work ahead of us.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了摆在我们面前的工作。

sentences.en: Everything changed.
sentences.zh: 一切都变了。

sentences.en: And the importance of bringing this country together.
sentences.zh: 以及凝聚这个国家的重要性。

sentences.en: Paul Ryan would now seem to have everything he needed back in 2009.
sentences.zh: 现在的保罗·瑞恩似乎拥有了他在2009年时所需的一切。

sentences.en: So why, as the House votes today on the Republican health care plan, is its fate so uncertain?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么在众议院今天对共和党医改方案进行投票时，它的命运却如此扑朔迷离？

sentences.en: Wait, so where are you?
sentences.zh: 等等，那你现在在哪？

sentences.en: They have these funny...
sentences.zh: 他们有这些有趣的……

sentences.en: In the Senate press gallery, they have five phone booths.
sentences.zh: 在参议院新闻发布厅里，有五个电话亭。

sentences.en: So it's the idea that you can go and have a private conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以这个概念就是你可以去那里进行私密的对话。

sentences.en: And there are landlines in there.
sentences.zh: 里面有固定电话。

sentences.en: Is this like an old wooden affair?
sentences.zh: 这是一种老式的木制装置吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I reached my colleague Jennifer Steinhauer in a phone booth in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我在美国国会大厦的一个电话亭里联系到了我的同事詹妮弗·斯坦豪尔。

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 国会山。

sentences.en: Jennifer, I just want to...
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗，我只想……

sentences.en: First of all, hello.
sentences.zh: 首先，你好。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Talk to me about how House Republicans are getting used to the idea of being in charge.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊众议院共和党人是如何适应掌权这一角色的。

sentences.en: So House Speaker Paul Ryan likes to say, we've got to stop being the party of opposition.
sentences.zh: 所以众议院议长保罗·瑞恩喜欢说，我们必须停止做反对党。

sentences.en: We've got to be a bold alternative party, a proposition party.
sentences.zh: 我们要成为一个勇敢的替代党，一个提案党。

sentences.en: And be the party of proposition, and be the party that runs things.
sentences.zh: 要做一个提出方案的党，要做一个掌权的党。

sentences.en: We need to find common ground where we can find it to advance the nation's interests, and we can do so...
sentences.zh: 我们需要在力所能及的范围内寻找共同点，以推进国家利益，我们能够做到这一点……

sentences.en: And this has actually been quite a difficult transition for a lot of House Republicans to make.
sentences.zh: 对于许多众议院共和党人来说，这实际上是一个相当艰难的转变过程。

sentences.en: Roughly two-thirds of the House Republican conference has never served under a Republican president.
sentences.zh: 大约三分之二的众议院共和党会议成员从未在共和党总统手下任职过。

sentences.en: They are trained and schooled, and some ran on the concept of running against Democrats and the Obama agenda.
sentences.zh: 他们受到的训练和教育，以及部分人的竞选理念就是与民主党和奥巴马的议程作对。

sentences.en: So now they've got a Republican president who ostensibly shares their agenda.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他们有了一位表面上与他们有着共同议程的共和党总统。

sentences.en: To do what?
sentences.zh: 要做什么？

sentences.en: Repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 废除并替代《平价医疗法案》。

sentences.en: And it's just the jury's really out where they can pull it off.
sentences.zh: 大家目前真的还拿不准他们究竟能不能成功办到。

sentences.en: Jennifer, I think this might be best if we break this down in terms of teaMs.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗，我觉得如果我们把这个按团队来划分的话可能会更好。

sentences.en: Can you roughly give me the names of three, maybe even four teams here among the House Republicans and who their key players are at the moment?
sentences.zh: 你能大致说出这里众议院共和党人中的三支、甚至四支队伍的名称，以及他们目前的关键人物分别是谁吗？

sentences.en: There's obviously...
sentences.zh: 显然有……

sentences.en: The key player is Paul Ryan and the majority leader, Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 关键人物是保罗·瑞恩和多数党领袖凯文·麦卡锡。

sentences.en: There's a leadership team, and their team is full of the Republican conference.
sentences.zh: 有一个领导团队，他们的团队由共和党会议成员组成。

sentences.en: Not enough to pass a bill, but a large swath of members from all across the country who've been aching to repeal Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 虽然人数不足以通过法案，但这是一大批来自全国各地、一直渴望废除奥巴马医改的议员。

sentences.en: The president of the United States came to us and said, We all made a promise to the American people, and we need to keep our promises.
sentences.zh: 美国总统来到我们面前说，我们都对美国人民做出过承诺，我们需要兑现承诺。

sentences.en: And we keep our promise, and the people will reward us.
sentences.zh: 我们兑现承诺，人民就会回报我们。

sentences.en: If we don't keep our promise, it will be very hard to manage this.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不兑现承诺，局面将很难控制。

sentences.en: Welcome, Senator.
sentences.zh: 欢迎，参议员。

sentences.en: What's wrong with this bill?
sentences.zh: 这个法案有什么问题？

sentences.en: I think it's basically Obamacare-like.
sentences.zh: 我认为它基本上就是奥巴马医改的翻版。

sentences.en: Who would like to go back to a time pre-Obamacare, or who would like to modify Obamacare down to its most bare bones?
sentences.zh: 谁愿意回到奥巴马医改之前的时代，或者谁愿意将奥巴马医改精简到最基础的骨架？

sentences.en: We do not agree with the fundamental three or four things that Ryan has.
sentences.zh: 我们不同意瑞恩提出的那三四个根本性问题。

sentences.en: Subsidies, taxes, mandates, and insurance bailout.
sentences.zh: 补贴、税收、强制规定和保险纾困。

sentences.en: That's Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 那就是奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: We don't want that.
sentences.zh: 我们不想要那样。

sentences.en: Then you have so-called moderates.
sentences.zh: 然后你有所谓的温和派。

sentences.en: In my state, I have 700,000 people who are included in the Medicaid expansion, and probably about a total of 1.1 million people who now have coverage.
sentences.zh: 在我的州，有70万人被纳入了医疗白卡扩容计划，总共大约有110万人现在拥有了保险。

sentences.en: I want to understand how these people are going to be impacted.
sentences.zh: 我想了解这些人将受到怎样的影响。

sentences.en: And at this point, those questions have not been answered satisfactorily for me.
sentences.zh: 但在这一点上，这些问题还没有得到令我满意的解答。

sentences.en: That are concerned about how their states will be affected in constituents in their districts, and how this will possibly punish them in their re-election efforts.
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己的州将如何受到影响、选区内的选民会受到什么影响，以及这是否会在他们的连任竞选中惩罚他们。

sentences.en: And you need the vast majority of all those teaMs.
sentences.zh: 你需要所有这些团队中的绝大多数人。

sentences.en: To get this bill passed.
sentences.zh: 才能让这个法案通过。

sentences.en: That's what we do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的做法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Jennifer, let's talk about these factions in a little more detail, starting with Paul Ryan.
sentences.zh: 那么，詹妮弗，让我们更详细地聊聊这些派别，从保罗·瑞恩开始。

sentences.en: What the House Republicans decided to do was try to go ahead and push this thing through, trying to fulfill the basic agenda of repealing the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 众议院共和党人决定做的是，直接强行推动这件事，试图实现废除《平价医疗法案》的基本议程。

sentences.en: And they didn't take the time and energy to build a broad coalition off of the hill.
sentences.zh: 而他们没有花时间和精力在国会山之外建立广泛的联盟。

sentences.en: Doctors don't like it.
sentences.zh: 医生不喜欢它。

sentences.en: Nurses don't like it.
sentences.zh: 护士不喜欢它。

sentences.en: The hospital association is actively pushing against it.
sentences.zh: 医院协会也在积极反对它。

sentences.en: And insurers have been lukewarm, if not negative.
sentences.zh: 保险公司的态度也顶多是不冷不热，甚至持否定态度。

sentences.en: On top of which, you have all kinds of traditional Republican groups, Heritage, Club for Growth, these groups that get financial support to members in elections,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，你有各种传统的共和党团体，比如传统基金会、增长俱乐部，这些在选举中为议员提供资金支持的团体，

sentences.en: but don't like the bill.
sentences.zh: 却并不喜欢这项法案。

sentences.en: Because they think that it's not going to improve insurance and premiuMs.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为这不会改善保险和保费状况。

sentences.en: And they think, at least in the short term, it'll increase insurance and premiums,
sentences.zh: 他们认为，至少在短期内，它会推高保险费和保费，

sentences.en: which they think will be difficult for Republicans trying to run for re-election in the House and Senate, and ultimately President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这对于试图在众议院、参议院寻求连任的共和党人以及最终的特朗普总统来说会很艰难。

sentences.en: So, you've got conservative groups.
sentences.zh: 所以，你既有保守派团体。

sentences.en: Obviously, you have Democrats and all liberal groups.
sentences.zh: 显然，你还有民主党人和所有自由派团体。

sentences.en: You have professional groups against it.
sentences.zh: 你还有反对它的专业团体。

sentences.en: There's no coalition there.
sentences.zh: 那里根本没有什么联盟可言。

sentences.en: And that's just really hard when you're trying to pass something as difficult as any type of health care bill.
sentences.zh: 当你试图通过任何类型的医改法案这样困难的事情时，这就真的很难办。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about how the opposition among House Republicans is breaking down.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们来谈谈众议院共和党内部的反对派是如何分裂的。

sentences.en: Let's begin with Republicans like Mark Meadows.
sentences.zh: 让我们从像马克·梅多斯这样的共和党人开始。

sentences.en: Who is Mark Meadows?
sentences.zh: 马克·梅多斯是谁？

sentences.en: And Donald Trump and I are not at odds.
sentences.zh: 我和唐纳德·特朗普并没有意见分歧。

sentences.en: We want to make sure that we repeal the Affordable Care Act and replace it with something that drives down health care costs.
sentences.zh: 我们希望确保废除《平价医疗法案》，并用能够降低医疗成本的方案取而代之。

sentences.en: Mark Meadows is a conservative guy for North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 马克·梅多斯是来自北卡罗来纳州的保守派人士。

sentences.en: And this doesn't do it.
sentences.zh: 而这个法案没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: He's in a very Republican district.
sentences.zh: 他所在的选区非常支持共和党。

sentences.en: He's reflecting the views of a lot of hardcore Republicans who would like to see far less government roles, certainly in the health care system.
sentences.zh: 他反映了许多核心共和党人的观点，他们希望看到政府扮演远为次要的角色，尤其是在医疗系统中。

sentences.en: And I would count him as somebody who is not to, by the way, dismiss his understanding of policy or his intellect.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我认为不能低估他对政策的理解或他的智商。

sentences.en: But he is among a group of lawmakers whose brand, if you will, is to vote no.
sentences.zh: 但他属于这样一群议员，他们的标签可以说就是投反对票。

sentences.en: It is time that the representatives start representing the people that they were elected to uphold and protect.
sentences.zh: 现在是代表们开始代表他们被选来维护和保护的人民的时候了。

sentences.en: They just like to be in opposition.
sentences.zh: 他们就是喜欢处于反对地位。

sentences.en: They've loved being in opposition, obviously, to Democrats and obviously to President Obama.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们一直很享受反对民主党、反对奥巴马总统的立场。

sentences.en: But they've also relished being in opposition to the establishment leaders of their party.
sentences.zh: 但他们同样津津乐道于反对自己党内的建制派领袖。

sentences.en: The government this, the government that, the government.
sentences.zh: 政府这个，政府那个，都是政府。

sentences.en: When do we start focusing on the people?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候开始把焦点放在人民身上？

sentences.en: Some of them tried to get rid of Speaker Bayer, and they ultimately succeeded.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有些人曾试图赶走议长博纳，并且最终成功了。

sentences.en: Some of them have even voted against the Speaker.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至对议长投了反对票。

sentences.en: In previous years, they just love being the opposition.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，他们就是热爱扮演反对派。

sentences.en: It's our position in the House Freedom Caucus that this plan, the current plan, doesn't go far enough.
sentences.zh: 我们众议院自由党团的立场是，这个计划，即当前的计划，还不够彻底。

sentences.en: They give themselves a name, right?
sentences.zh: 他们给自己取了个名字，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, a core group of them is called the House Freedom Caucus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们中的核心集团被称为众议院自由党团。

sentences.en: And they do meet, and they meet, and they have their own rules and their own peculiar, specific ways of voting together.
sentences.zh: 他们确实会开会，不断开会，并且有他们自己的规则和独特、具体的共同投票方式。

sentences.en: And when they vote is a block, and when they don't vote is a block.
sentences.zh: 他们投票时是一个整体，不投票时也是一个整体。

sentences.en: They have a weekly meeting called Conversations with the Conservatives, where they invite the media in to discuss various issues.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个名为“与保守派对话”的每周会议，在会上他们会邀请媒体来讨论各种议题。

sentences.en: It's catchy.
sentences.zh: 挺顺口的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They usually serve Chick-fil-A, sometimes pizza.
sentences.zh: 他们通常会提供福来鸡，有时是披萨。

sentences.en: So they've tried very hard to be a relevant thorn in the side of the Speaker, and they've often succeeded.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们非常努力地成为议长身边一个令人头疼的焦点，而且他们经常成功。

sentences.en: So what do Freedom Caucus members like Congressman Meadows say about this particular Republican health care bill?
sentences.zh: 那么像梅多斯国会议员这样的自由党团成员对这个特定的共和党医改法案怎么看？

sentences.en: Oh, it doesn't do enough to save the government money.
sentences.zh: 哦，它在为政府省钱方面做得还不够。

sentences.en: It still has too many mandates.
sentences.zh: 它里面还是有太多的强制规定。

sentences.en: But, you know, you ask, you know, what does a House Freedom Caucus member want?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果你去问，众议院自由党团成员到底想要什么？

sentences.en: And it's kind of hard to know, because they move the goalposts and usually vote no anyway.
sentences.zh: 其实很难知道，因为他们总是在移动目标，而且无论如何通常都会投反对票。

sentences.en: And this is the Lucy football situation that John Boehner would get into, where he would listen, and he would try to do some things to appease them.
sentences.zh: 这就成了约翰·博纳曾经陷入的那种露西踢橄榄球的局面：他会去倾听，并尝试做一些事情来安抚他们。

sentences.en: And often they would just vote against him anyway.
sentences.zh: 但通常他们最后还是会投反对票来对抗他。

sentences.en: So when you are a block, you have the power of the vote.
sentences.zh: 所以当你作为一个整体时，你就拥有投票的力量。

sentences.en: One individual member, not so powerful.
sentences.zh: 单个议员的力量其实并不那么强大。

sentences.en: Voting together, powerful.
sentences.zh: 但团结起来投票，力量就很强大。

sentences.en: So then there's a congressman like Charlie Dent.
sentences.zh: 那么还有像查理·登特这样的国会议员。

sentences.en: What's going to happen with this health care law is this.
sentences.zh: 这项医疗保健法接下来会这样发展。

sentences.en: Parts of it need to be repealed.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分需要被废除。

sentences.en: Parts of it need to be replaced.
sentences.zh: 一部分需要被替换。

sentences.en: Parts of it need to be overhauled and reformed.
sentences.zh: 一部分需要被彻底修改和重组。

sentences.en: Who is Charlie Dent?
sentences.zh: 查理·登特是谁？

sentences.en: And other parts will be maintained.
sentences.zh: 而其他部分则会保留。

sentences.en: He would probably describe himself as a center-right Republican from Pennsylvania who has constituents who are obviously enrolled in a bond care.
sentences.zh: 他大概会把自己描述为来自宾夕法尼亚州的中右翼共和党人，他的选民显然有人参加了某种医疗补助计划。

sentences.en: And he would like to repeal the law, as most Republicans would.
sentences.zh: 正如大多数共和党人一样，他也希望废除这项法律。

sentences.en: But he wants to do it in a way that is not particularly fully on board with everything that Paul Ryan wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 但他希望以一种并非完全赞同保罗·瑞安想要做的一切的方式来做。

sentences.en: So he wants to reflect the needs of his state.
sentences.zh: 所以他希望反映自己所在州的需求。

sentences.en: And that would be something that protects people who are in the Medicaid program currently.
sentences.zh: 这将是某种能够保护目前正处于医疗补助计划中的人们的方案。

sentences.en: And that has structured in a way that if you are losing your health care insurance, the tax credits are sufficient,
sentences.zh: 并且其结构设计是这样的：如果你失去了医疗保险，税收抵免将是充足的，

sentences.en: particularly for groups of older Americans who are too young to qualify for Medicare,
sentences.zh: 特别是对于那些年纪太小而无法获得联邦医疗保险资格的老年美国人群体，

sentences.en: but have low enough incomes that they've been able to benefit from some of the Medicaid prograMs.
sentences.zh: 但他们的收入又足够低，以至于他们一直能够受益于某些医疗补助计划。

sentences.en: And these lower income Americans who are not quite Medicare eligible are a huge concern for a lot of Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这些收入较低且尚未达到联邦医疗保险资格的美国人是许多共和党人格外关注的巨大问题。

sentences.en: So President Trump met with many of these moderate House Republicans on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普总统周二会见了许多这些温和派众议院共和党人。

sentences.en: And usually the power of a president in this case might be to issue threats and cajole.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，总统的权力通常可能是发出威胁和进行哄骗。

sentences.en: But these are moderates and they may not really care.
sentences.zh: 但这些人是温和派，他们可能并不真正在乎。

sentences.en: And their voters may not really care what President Trump may threaten or not threaten them to do.
sentences.zh: 他们的选民也可能并不在乎特朗普总统对他们进行什么威胁或不威胁。

sentences.en: So what do you think President Trump's message to this particular group is?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为特朗普总统对这个特定群体的信息是什么？

sentences.en: When President Trump met with the so-called Tuesday group, which are a group of, they call themselves, Center Right of Moderate Republicans and others,
sentences.zh: 当特朗普总统会见所谓的周二小组时——这是一群自称为中右翼或温和派共和党人及其他人员的团体——

sentences.en: he mostly listened to their concerns.
sentences.zh: 他主要是在倾听他们的关切。

sentences.en: He didn't try to arm twiSt.
sentences.zh: 他没有试图施压扭转。

sentences.en: It's different than how it was in the morning when he came to the Capitol and really pressed members in a conference-wide meeting, kind of made vague threats of primary challenges,
sentences.zh: 这不同于早上的情况，当时他来到国会大厦，在全体会议上真正向议员施压，对初选挑战做出了某种模糊的威胁，

sentences.en: and really cajoled, begged, you know, in his way to vote for the bill.
sentences.zh: 并且以他自己的方式真正进行了哄骗和恳求，让他们投票支持该法案。

sentences.en: This was much more listening.
sentences.zh: 这一次更多的是倾听。

sentences.en: The problem with that method is that President Trump, by all accounts of people who have met with him, does not get into the weeds of policy.
sentences.zh: 这种方法的问题在于，据所有见过特朗普总统的人所说，他并不深入钻研政策细节。

sentences.en: So these very specific complaints they were making may not have resonated with him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们提出的这些非常具体的抱怨可能并没有引起他的共鸣。

sentences.en: And, you know, some of these members, Trump won their state, sure, won their district, but they did better than he did in their district or their state.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，其中一些议员所在的州特朗普赢了，没错，他们的选区特朗普也赢了，但他们在自己选区或自己州的表现比特朗普还要好。

sentences.en: And when the president has, what, a 37% approval rating?
sentences.zh: 当总统的支持率只有百分之多少，比如37%时？

sentences.en: That's not necessarily a scary hammer.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是一个可怕的大棒。

sentences.en: It's just a hammer.
sentences.zh: 它只是一把锤子。

sentences.en: It's a hammer.
sentences.zh: 它只是一把锤子。

sentences.en: So we talked about these conservatives who just can't get behind this.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了这些根本无法支持该法案的保守派。

sentences.en: And then we've talked about these moderates who just can't get behind this.
sentences.zh: 然后我们又讨论了这些根本无法支持该法案的温和派。

sentences.en: If you had to say of Trump that he was a member of one of these factions, where would you put him?
sentences.zh: 如果你必须说特朗普是其中某一个派系的成员，你会把他归入哪里？

sentences.en: I can't put him anywhere because he still continues to campaign as a populiSt.
sentences.zh: 我无法把他归入任何地方，因为他仍然继续以民粹主义者的身份进行竞选。

sentences.en: And he fills his cabinet with conservatives, right?
sentences.zh: 而且他的内阁塞满了保守派，对吧？

sentences.en: And then he sends out a budget that's neither.
sentences.zh: 然后他发布了一份两边都不靠的预算案。

sentences.en: So he's, when people say Trump Republican, that will mean something at some point.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们说“特朗普式共和党人”时，在某个时候这会有所含义。

sentences.en: Really definitive.
sentences.zh: 非常明确的含义。

sentences.en: Just like we had Reagan Democrats, Trump Republicans, it'll have a meaning.
sentences.zh: 就像我们曾经有里根民主党人一样，特朗普式共和党人也会有它的含义。

sentences.en: We're not quite there yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没完全到那一步。

sentences.en: What does, no Republican can define him.
sentences.zh: 没有任何共和党人能定义他。

sentences.en: He's defining them.
sentences.zh: 反而是他在定义他们。

sentences.en: And what team is Donald Trump on?
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普到底站在哪一边？

sentences.en: Donald Trump just wants to win.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普只想赢。

sentences.en: He's not interested in the names of the players or the jerseys.
sentences.zh: 他对球员的名字或球衣不感兴趣。

sentences.en: He just wants to see the scoreboard light, say Trump won.
sentences.zh: 他只想看到记分牌亮起，上面写着特朗普赢了。

sentences.en: We are going to repeal and replace horrible, disastrous Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 我们将要废除并取代这个可怕、灾难性的奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: The bill that I will ultimately sign.
sentences.zh: 我最终将签署的法案。

sentences.en: And that will be a bill where everybody's going to get into the room and we're going to get it done.
sentences.zh: 那将是一项让每个人都进入房间并把它做成的法案。

sentences.en: We'll get rid of Obamacare and make health care better for you and for your family.
sentences.zh: 我们将摆脱奥巴马医改，为妳和妳的家人带来更好的医疗保健。

sentences.en: And, you know, make no mistake, Republicans up here on Capitol Hill are dying to have a unified conservative agenda with the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，毫无疑问，国会山这里的共和党人极度渴望与美利坚合众国总统达成统一的保守派议程。

sentences.en: They want this marriage to work.
sentences.zh: 他们希望这场“婚姻”能够成功。

sentences.en: They want this marriage to work.
sentences.zh: 他们希望这场“婚姻”能够成功。

sentences.en: They just need their partner to engage a little more.
sentences.zh: 他们只是需要他们的伴侣多投入一点。

sentences.en: More communication, Michael.
sentences.zh: 更多的沟通，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Like a good marriage.
sentences.zh: 就像一段美满的婚姻一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thank you, folks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Jennifer, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Good luck.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The Republican bill needs 216 votes to pass today.
sentences.zh: 共和党的法案今天需要216票才能通过。

sentences.en: On Wednesday night, 148 Republicans had said they would likely support it.
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，有148名共和党人表示他们可能会支持它。

sentences.en: 27 had said they would not.
sentences.zh: 27人表示不会支持。

sentences.en: And 62 were undecided, had concerns or had not said how they'd vote.
sentences.zh: 还有62人尚未决定、有所顾虑或未表态将如何投票。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听播客节目《重塑者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的节目。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，你每天晚上也要带着300件你最珍贵的传家宝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的、犹如展示50年历史精美老物件的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: Subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today, and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 订阅《纽约时报》，立即下载时报应用程序，即可免费获得30天访问权限。

sentences.en: Just after 2.30 this afternoon, Terror returned to the streets of London.
sentences.zh: 今天下午2点30分刚过，恐怖再次降临伦敦街头。

sentences.en: In the first stage of a two-pronged attack, a car plowed into pedestrians on Westminster Bridge.
sentences.zh: 在双管齐下的袭击的第一阶段，一辆汽车在威斯敏斯特桥上撞向行人。

sentences.en: The car traveled around the corner, crashing into railings outside the Houses of Parliament,
sentences.zh: 汽车转过街角，撞上了议会大厦外的栏杆，

sentences.en: where the driver, apparently armed with two knives, attacked a policeman before being shot by armed officers.
sentences.zh: 司机显然手持两把刀，在那里袭击了一名警察，随后被武装警察开枪击中。

sentences.en: Both the policeman and his assailant died.
sentences.zh: 警察和袭击者双双身亡。

sentences.en: So, you know, we heard about it when we were in our offices.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们是在办公室里听到这个消息的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I immediately grabbed my bike, I cycled down there, and I was there before 3 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我立刻抓起我的自行车，骑车赶往那里，在3点钟之前就到了现场。

sentences.en: I mean, this happened around 2.40.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这件事发生在2点40分左右。

sentences.en: My colleague Katrin Benhold lives in London and is reporting on Wednesday's attack.
sentences.zh: 我的同事卡特琳·本霍尔德住在伦敦，正在报道周三的袭击事件。

sentences.en: I talked to eyewitnesses who were describing a sort of people littered across the Westminster Bridge.
sentences.zh: 我采访了目击者，他们描述威斯敏斯特桥上横七竖八地躺着一些人。

sentences.en: And then that one person who had been killed very near the railings itself.
sentences.zh: 然后就是那个在栏杆附近遇害的人。

sentences.en: There was a group of students who, you know, three of whom, from France, actually, three of whom were injured.
sentences.zh: 有一群学生，其中三人——实际上来自法国，其中三人受伤了。

sentences.en: And one woman who was believed to have fallen or plunged into the Thames and is very severely injured.
sentences.zh: 还有一名据信坠入泰晤士河的女性，伤势非常严重。

sentences.en: You know, the thing that I'm most struck about is actually the stoicism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最让我震撼的其实是那种坚忍不拔的精神。

sentences.en: You know, the sort of World War II motto that was born during German bombardments and the Blitz, you know, the whole kind of keep calm and carry on,
sentences.zh: 你知道，二战时期在德国轰炸和闪电战期间诞生的座右铭，你知道，那种“保持冷静，继续前行”的精神，

sentences.en: which has defined Britain's ever since.
sentences.zh: 这种精神此后一直定义着英国。

sentences.en: It's kind of a caricature and it's such imperfect, but it was really unimpressive to play today.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是一种刻画，而且很不完美，但今天它的表现确实令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: After the first initial panic had subsided, people were just getting on with it.
sentences.zh: 在最初的恐慌消退后，人们只是在继续他们的生活。

sentences.en: And there was, you know, one woman, for example, who owns a newsstand, which has been in the ownership of her family for nearly 100 years.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，有一位女性经营着一家报摊，她的家族拥有这家报摊已近百年。

sentences.en: Kirsten Hurl was telling me that she pretty much saw the car careering across the cycle line and into the railings of Parliament right underneath Big Bend.
sentences.zh: 柯尔斯滕·赫尔告诉我，她亲眼看到汽车冲过自行车道，撞进大本钟正下方的议会栏杆。

sentences.en: And, you know, I asked her how she felt about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我问她对此有何感受。

sentences.en: You know, she was the one who called the emergency service.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她是那个拨打紧急服务电话的人。

sentences.en: I said, were you panicked?
sentences.zh: 我说，你们当时恐慌吗？

sentences.en: Were you afraid?
sentences.zh: 你们害怕吗？

sentences.en: And she said, no, none of the above.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，以上都没有。

sentences.en: She said, I lived through the IRA.
sentences.zh: 她说，我经历过爱尔兰共和军时期。

sentences.en: So there's a sense in the city that is lived through so much already that they need to pull together now and get on with it.
sentences.zh: 所以这座城市有一种经历过风雨的感觉，他们现在需要团结起来，继续生活。

sentences.en: And I was struck myself by receiving an email from Parliament itself this evening that the House of Lords and the House of Commons will sit as normal tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 今晚我收到议会本身发来的一封电子邮件，这让我感到震惊，邮件称上议院和下议院明天将照常开会。

sentences.en: So I think the mood is defiant.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种情绪是反抗的。

sentences.en: There's a sense of solidarity.
sentences.zh: 有一种团结一致的感觉。

sentences.en: And Londoners are basically saying we're standing together.
sentences.zh: 伦敦人基本上在说我们站在一起。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Prime Minister Theresa May said today, the attacker struck at the heart of the city.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，首相特雷莎·梅今天表示，袭击者打击了这座城市的心脏。

sentences.en: And it's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He did get pretty close to the center of British government, which I think was the shock to a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 他确实非常接近英国政府的中心，我认为这对很多人来说是个震撼。

sentences.en: It was right there.
sentences.zh: 它就在那里。

sentences.en: You know, the symbols of power and pride.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是权力和骄傲的象征。

sentences.en: The car that went down, several people on the bridge crashed into the railings right underneath Big Bend.
sentences.zh: 那辆冲下桥撞向大本钟正下方栏杆的汽车载有好几个人。

sentences.en: I mean, there is no more symbolic monument in London.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，伦敦再也没有比这更具象征意义的纪念碑了。

sentences.en: It's like the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
sentences.zh: 它就像巴黎的埃菲尔铁塔一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The first thing you think of when you think of London.
sentences.zh: 当你想到伦敦时，你首先想到的就是它。

sentences.en: You know, the one thing I was quite struck by, because we've been focusing on Brexit and these kind of very politically polarizing times we're in right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一件事让我相当震撼，因为我们一直专注于英国脱欧以及我们目前身处这种政治两极分化的时代。

sentences.en: And today was a day for all its strategy that actually humanized the kind of center of government here, which has been, you know,
sentences.zh: 而今天这一天，尽管有种种策略，却实际上让人情味涌现，拉近了这里政府中心的距离，这里一直是，你知道的，

sentences.en: the kind of Westminster is a bit a byword for the distant elite who don't understand ordinary people, quite in the same way that Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 威斯敏斯特有点像是高高在上、不理解普通人的遥远精英的代名词，这与华盛顿特区

sentences.en: probably is in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在美国的情况很像。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And today, just the images of a member of parliament, Tobias Elwood, actually trying to resuscitate this policeman who's been stabbed, you know,
sentences.zh: 而今天，仅仅是国会议员托比亚斯·埃尔伍德试图对这名被刺伤的警察进行心肺复苏的画面，你知道的，

sentences.en: with blood on his face and his hands, hands on, you know, a human being with various MPs giving their accounts of the scene because they were right there and experienced it.
sentences.zh: 他的脸和手上都沾满了鲜血，亲力亲为，作为一个有血有肉的人，其他议员也纷纷讲述现场的见闻，因为他们就在现场并亲身经历了这一切。

sentences.en: I think it was a moment, and it probably won't last, they rarely do,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个时刻，虽然可能不会持久，它们很少能持久，

sentences.en: but it was a moment where the country did come together and where divisions that have been on such display in recent weeks and months were actually buried under that sort of sense of solidarity.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个国家凝聚在一起的时刻，在最近几周和几个月里表现得淋漓尽致的分歧，实际上都被那种团结感所掩盖了。

sentences.en: I thought that was quite striking as well.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得这相当震撼。

sentences.en: Tomorrow morning, Parliament will meet as normal.
sentences.zh: 明天早上，议会将照常开会。

sentences.en: We will come together as normal.
sentences.zh: 我们将照常聚在一起。

sentences.en: And Londoners and others from around the world who have come here to visit this great city will get up and go about their day as normal.
sentences.zh: 伦敦人以及来自世界各地造访这座伟大城市的其他人将起身并照常开始他们的日常生活。

sentences.en: And we will all move forward together, never giving in to terror.
sentences.zh: 我们将携手向前迈进，绝不向恐怖主义屈服。

sentences.en: British police are calling this a terrorist attack, the most serious in London since the deadly subway bombings in July of 2005.
sentences.zh: 英国警方称这是一起恐怖袭击，是自2005年7月致命地铁爆炸案以来伦敦最严重的一次。

sentences.en: British Prime Minister Theresa May has said that the attack was carried out by just one man, the assailant killed by police outside of Parliament.
sentences.zh: 英国首相特雷莎·梅表示，袭击是由一名男子实施的，袭击者在议会大楼外被警方击毙。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他事情。

sentences.en: On his third and final day of testimony in front of the Senate, President Trump's Supreme Court nominee, Neil Gorsuch,
sentences.zh: 在参议院进行第三天也是最后一天作证时，特朗普总统提名的最高法院大法官人选尼尔·戈萨奇

sentences.en: faced tough questions about his work for former President George W.
sentences.zh: 面临着关于他在9·11袭击后为前总统乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush after the September 11th attacks.
sentences.zh: 布什工作经历的严厉质问。

sentences.en: My question is, what information did you have that the Bush administration's aggressive interrogation techniques were effective?
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，你有什么信息表明布什政府的激进审讯技术是有效的？

sentences.en: At the height of the war on terror, Gorsuch was a lawyer for the Bush administration as it wrestled with controversial questions about abuse of detainees and torture.
sentences.zh: 在反恐战争的高峰期，戈萨奇曾担任布什政府的律师，当时政府正在艰难应对有关虐待被关押人员和酷刑的争议问题。

sentences.en: And Senator, I'm working on 12 years of passage of time here.
sentences.zh: 议员先生，这里已经过去了12年时间。

sentences.en: My memory is what it is.
sentences.zh: 我的记忆也就是这样。

sentences.en: And it's not great on this, but my recollection.
sentences.zh: 在这方面不是很好，但这是我的回忆。

sentences.en: But you're very young.
sentences.zh: 但你非常年轻。

sentences.en: Well.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Accept it.
sentences.zh: 接受它。

sentences.en: I'll take it.
sentences.zh: 我接受了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Gorsuch's testimony is now complete.
sentences.zh: 戈尔萨奇的听证会现在已经结束。

sentences.en: The Senate Judiciary Committee will vote on his confirmation on April 3rd.
sentences.zh: 参议院司法委员会将于4月3日对他的提名进行表决。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日秀》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时扣人心弦的争斗之中。
